title: SailPoint Engineer Domain 8 questions (8.1, 8.2)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: An engineer is preparing next week's quarterly manager campaign. Reviewers must see each person's access as it is today, not as it was last month. What should the engineer do FIRST?
choices: Raise the priority of every identity profile in the tenant
Run fresh account and entitlement aggregations on the in-scope sources
Turn off access requests until the campaign has been completed
Delete last quarter's completed campaigns so their old data is not reused again
questions.answer: Run fresh account and entitlement aggregations on the in-scope sources
questions.explanation: Campaigns are built from the access data already in the tenant, so current aggregations are the key preparation step. Deleting old campaigns does not refresh any account or entitlement data.

questions.stem: In last year's campaign, reviewers complained that Active Directory groups appeared only as long technical names they could not interpret. What is the BEST preparation before the next campaign?
choices: Convert every Active Directory group into its own role before generating it
Require reviewers to reauthenticate before they can approve any item
Switch the campaign to a source owner campaign so only IT staff review it
Give the entitlements clear display names and descriptions first
questions.answer: Give the entitlements clear display names and descriptions first
questions.explanation: Reviewers make better decisions when entitlements carry business-friendly names and descriptions. Changing the campaign type only moves the confusing names to different reviewers.

questions.stem: A company is running its first certification campaign across 40,000 identities. The governance lead worries about mistakes reaching every manager at once. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Launch the full campaign at once and fix any problems as reviewers report them
Skip the preview so the campaign reflects the very latest data
Run a pilot campaign for one department first and check its preview carefully
Set a one-day deadline so mistakes are exposed to managers quickly
questions.answer: Run a pilot campaign for one department first and check its preview carefully
questions.explanation: A small pilot scoped by filter or search exposes data and reviewer problems before they reach the whole workforce. Launching everything at once makes every error visible to every manager.

questions.stem: Before launching a manager campaign, an engineer wants a list of the identities that would be left out because no manager is defined. Which report should the engineer download?
choices: The Campaign Remediation Status report
The Access Request Activity report
The Identities Without Managers report
The Certification Sign Off report
questions.answer: The Identities Without Managers report
questions.explanation: Identities without a manager are excluded from manager campaigns, and the Identities Without Managers report lists them. The remediation status report covers revocations after a campaign runs.

questions.stem: An engineer plans a source owner campaign covering six sources. Two of the sources were onboarded recently by a contractor. What should the engineer verify before creating the campaign?
choices: That each of the six sources has an account deletion threshold set
That each of the six sources has delta aggregation enabled
That each of the six sources has the correct source owner assigned
That each of the six sources is linked to an identity profile
questions.answer: That each of the six sources has the correct source owner assigned
questions.explanation: Source owner campaigns route reviews to source owners and only generate for sources that have owners assigned. Delta aggregation and deletion thresholds do not decide who reviews.

questions.stem: Managers say past campaigns had hundreds of low-risk birthright items each and they approved everything without reading. What is the BEST change for the next campaign?
choices: Add a second reviewer so every item is approved by two managers
Send daily reminders until every manager has signed off
Extend the deadline so that managers have more time to read and approve each item
Use campaign filters to focus on higher-risk access and leave out birthright items
questions.answer: Use campaign filters to focus on higher-risk access and leave out birthright items
questions.explanation: Campaign filters cut review volume so reviewers can focus on access that matters, which reduces rubber-stamping. A longer deadline or a second reviewer leaves the same volume of low-value items in place.

questions.stem: A ticketing application source has 300 accounts that never correlated to identities. A manager campaign starts next week. What should the engineer do so the right managers review this access?
choices: Delete the uncorrelated accounts from the source so the campaign stays clean
Fix the correlation so these accounts link to their identities first
Add the uncorrelated accounts to a governance group for the campaign
Make the ticketing application authoritative in a new identity profile
questions.answer: Fix the correlation so these accounts link to their identities first
questions.explanation: Manager campaigns review access held by identities, so accounts must correlate before they can be routed to a manager. Making a ticketing app authoritative would create bogus identities.

questions.stem: Line managers must confirm that each direct report still needs all of their access across every connected system. Which campaign type BEST fits this requirement?
choices: Manager campaign
Search campaign scoped to one source
Source owner campaign
Role composition campaign
questions.answer: Manager campaign
questions.explanation: A manager campaign sends each manager the access of their direct reports across sources. A source owner campaign is organized by system, not by reporting line.

questions.stem: Auditors want the owner of a licensed trading application to review everyone's access to that application and nothing else. Which campaign type BEST fits?
choices: A manager campaign filtered to the trading department's managers
A role composition campaign for the roles that contain trading access
A manager campaign that includes every source in the tenant
A source owner campaign that includes only the trading application's source
questions.answer: A source owner campaign that includes only the trading application's source
questions.explanation: Source owner campaigns let the owner of one or more selected sources review access on those sources, which suits tightly controlled or licensed applications. Manager campaigns spread the review across managers.

questions.stem: A role owner says she does not want to decide who holds the Payroll Clerk role. She wants to confirm that the role still contains the right access and membership criteria. Which campaign type fits?
choices: Source owner campaign
Role composition campaign
Identity search campaign with the manager as reviewer
Manager campaign
questions.answer: Role composition campaign
questions.explanation: A role composition campaign reviews what a role contains, such as its access and membership criteria. The other types review which identities hold access, not the role's design.

questions.stem: Compliance needs a review of only the Finance department identities who hold privileged access on two specific sources. Which approach BEST builds this campaign?
choices: Create a source owner campaign for every source in the tenant
Create a campaign from a Search query that targets those identities
Create a role composition campaign for the Finance roles
Create a manager campaign and ask non-Finance managers to approve all items
questions.answer: Create a campaign from a Search query that targets those identities
questions.explanation: Search campaigns use a query to target a precise set of identities and access items. A source owner campaign for every source reviews far more than the requirement.

questions.stem: Some contractors have no manager in the tenant, but policy says every contractor's access must still get a manager-style review. Which approach includes them?
choices: A Search campaign with Manager as reviewer, which sends them to the campaign creator
A role composition campaign, which reviews contractor roles instead of people
A source owner campaign, which sends every identity to the owner of the HR source
A manager campaign, which sends any identity without a manager to the source owner instead
questions.answer: A Search campaign with Manager as reviewer, which sends them to the campaign creator
questions.explanation: Manager campaigns exclude identities without a manager, but a Search campaign with Manager as reviewer includes them and routes them to the campaign creator. Source owner campaigns do not review by reporting line.

questions.stem: A SOX control requires the owner of each sensitive access item to review who holds it, whichever department the holders are in. Which design BEST fits?
choices: A Search campaign for those access items with Access Owner as the reviewer
A source owner campaign for the sources of the sensitive items
A manager campaign filtered to include only the sensitive access items
A role composition campaign for every role in the tenant
questions.answer: A Search campaign for those access items with Access Owner as the reviewer
questions.explanation: Search campaigns can target specific access items and assign the access owner as reviewer. A source owner campaign routes reviews to whoever owns the source, not to the owner of each item.

questions.stem: Which campaign types does an admin create directly from Admin > Certifications > Campaigns, rather than starting from Search?
choices: Manager and source owner campaigns
Source owner and identity search campaigns
Manager and role composition campaigns
Role composition and access item campaigns
questions.answer: Manager and source owner campaigns
questions.explanation: The campaign creation page offers Manager Campaign and Source Owner Campaign. Identity, access item and role composition campaigns are started from Search.

questions.stem: A manager campaign should not ask managers to review the All Employees distribution group, which every worker receives. What is the BEST way to keep it out of the campaign?
choices: Mark the entitlement as not requestable in the access request settings
Remove the entitlement from every identity before the campaign starts
Ask managers to approve that item in bulk once the campaign starts
Apply a campaign filter that excludes that entitlement
questions.answer: Apply a campaign filter that excludes that entitlement
questions.explanation: Campaign filters limit a campaign to a subset of entitlements or users, so low-value access can be excluded. Making an item not requestable has no effect on certifications.

questions.stem: In an access item campaign with Access Owner as the reviewer, an entitlement has no owner and is not part of any role or access profile. Who is MOST likely to receive its review?
choices: The manager of each identity
The org admin who started the campaign
The owner of the entitlement's source
The campaign's assigned remediation owner
questions.answer: The owner of the entitlement's source
questions.explanation: When the access item has no owner, the reviewer falls through the ownership hierarchy, ending with the source owner. Managers are not part of the access owner hierarchy.

questions.stem: An engineer created a Search campaign with Manager as the reviewer. Twelve identities in the query have no manager defined. What happens to their reviews?
choices: They are dropped from the campaign entirely
They are approved automatically when the campaign starts
They are assigned to the owner of the authoritative source
They are assigned to the creator of the campaign
questions.answer: They are assigned to the creator of the campaign
questions.explanation: In Search campaigns with Manager as reviewer, an identity with no defined manager is reassigned to the campaign creator. Dropping identities without managers is what a manager campaign does.

questions.stem: A campaign preview shows an error next to one certification because the reviewer's identity no longer exists in the tenant. What should the admin do before starting the campaign?
choices: Reassign that certification to an existing identity from the preview
Recreate the reviewer's identity from an old account export
Change the campaign type to source owner and regenerate it
Start the campaign and let the reviewer's certification time out
questions.answer: Reassign that certification to an existing identity from the preview
questions.explanation: The preview lets admins reassign certifications, and a missing reviewer must be replaced with a valid identity. Starting anyway leaves those items without anyone able to review them.

questions.stem: A preview shows one manager assigned 2,000 identities because an HR feed error set the same manager for an entire region. What is the BEST action?
choices: Start the campaign and let that manager delegate the reviews informally
Reassign all 2,000 reviews to the campaign creator and then start the campaign as is
Extend the campaign deadline so the one manager can finish the reviews
Fix the manager data, refresh identities, then delete and regenerate the campaign
questions.answer: Fix the manager data, refresh identities, then delete and regenerate the campaign
questions.explanation: Campaigns are generated as a snapshot, so the source data must be fixed and the campaign regenerated to route reviews correctly. Moving everything to the creator hides the data problem instead of fixing it.

questions.stem: In a role composition campaign, a role owner revokes an access profile from the Sales Rep role. Who acts on that revocation?
choices: Each member's manager, who must approve the change to the role
The source owner, who edits the role on the source system
The connector, which removes the access profile from every account
The remediation owner, who gets a task to update the role manually
questions.answer: The remediation owner, who gets a task to update the role manually
questions.explanation: Role composition campaigns name an org or role admin as remediation owner, and revoked items become tasks for that person to update the role. Nothing is removed automatically from accounts.

questions.stem: Auditors require a written justification for every revoke decision in a campaign. What should the engineer configure?
choices: A governance group as the second reviewer for every certification
The campaign's comment setting so that reviewers must comment when they revoke
A campaign filter that excludes items with no description
Reauthenticated approvals for every access profile in the tenant
questions.answer: The campaign's comment setting so that reviewers must comment when they revoke
questions.explanation: Campaign settings let the admin choose when reviewers must leave comments on their decisions. Reauthenticated approvals apply to access requests, not to certification comments.

questions.stem: An engineer generated a campaign preview on Monday but could not start it until the following Tuesday. What does SailPoint recommend?
choices: Start the campaign, because previews refresh automatically when started
Run an identity refresh and then start the existing campaign
Delete the campaign and recreate it so its content is current
Extend the deadline by one week and then start the existing campaign
questions.answer: Delete the campaign and recreate it so its content is current
questions.explanation: SailPoint advises starting a campaign within a day of generating its preview, otherwise deleting and recreating it, because the content is a snapshot. An identity refresh does not update the generated campaign.

questions.stem: A new manager joined after a manager campaign was generated, and she cannot see reviews for her new team. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: Manager campaigns only include managers who existed when the template was saved
Managers can only see reviews after their first identity refresh of the month
Campaigns are a snapshot, so manager changes after generation are not reflected
New managers must be added to the Cert Admin user level first
questions.answer: Campaigns are a snapshot, so manager changes after generation are not reflected
questions.explanation: Campaigns are generated as a snapshot in time, so managers added afterwards do not appear. The Cert Admin user level is for administering certifications, not for reviewing.

questions.stem: A reviewer revokes an entitlement on a delimited file source that has no provisioning connector. How is that revocation carried out?
choices: The revocation is discarded because the source cannot provision
The virtual appliance edits the delimited file and uploads the new version again
The entitlement is removed during the next account aggregation
A manual task is created for a person to remove the access on the target system
questions.answer: A manual task is created for a person to remove the access on the target system
questions.explanation: Sources without automated provisioning get manual work items so someone removes the access by hand. Aggregation only reads data; it never removes access on the target.

questions.stem: A reviewer marked several items as revoke a week ago, yet none of the access has been removed. Her certification shows that it has not been signed off. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Revocations are processed only during the nightly identity refresh
Revocations are only processed after the campaign deadline passes
Revocations always need source owner approval before provisioning
Decisions are not final until the reviewer signs off on the certification
questions.answer: Decisions are not final until the reviewer signs off on the certification
questions.explanation: Reviewers must decide every item and sign off before their decisions are finalized and remediation starts. Waiting for the deadline is not what releases revocations.

questions.stem: An admin returns to a campaign that was generated but never started and finds its due date has already passed. What can the admin do with it?
choices: Start it as a staged campaign that reviewers can only view
It cannot be started, so the admin should delete it and create a new campaign
Convert it into a campaign template and start it from the template
Start it, and the deadline moves forward by two weeks automatically
questions.answer: It cannot be started, so the admin should delete it and create a new campaign
questions.explanation: A campaign whose due date has passed cannot be started, so it must be recreated. The deadline does not move forward automatically.

questions.stem: Halfway through a campaign, a reviewer goes on extended leave and has not opened her certification. What should the Cert Admin do?
choices: Delete the campaign and generate a new one without her
Approve all of her remaining items in bulk on her behalf
Reassign her certification to another suitable reviewer
Wait for the deadline so her items are revoked automatically
questions.answer: Reassign her certification to another suitable reviewer
questions.explanation: Admins can reassign a certification to another reviewer while the campaign runs. Approving on someone's behalf defeats the purpose of the review.

questions.stem: When creating a manager campaign, an admin leaves the Deadline field at its default value. When is the campaign due?
choices: Two weeks after the creation date
Thirty days after the creation date
One week after the creation date
At the end of the current calendar quarter
questions.answer: Two weeks after the creation date
questions.explanation: The default deadline is two weeks after the campaign is created. Admins can choose a different deadline when the review needs more or less time.

questions.stem: Every new hire receives an Email Basic access profile through the Active lifecycle state, but managers do not see it in their manager campaign. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The access profile has no owner, so it is filtered out of every certification campaign
Access profiles granted through lifecycle states are not included in manager campaigns
The managers have not been given the Cert Admin user level
Lifecycle state access is only certified in role composition campaigns
questions.answer: Access profiles granted through lifecycle states are not included in manager campaigns
questions.explanation: Access profiles granted through lifecycle states are left out of manager campaigns. Role composition campaigns review roles, not lifecycle state assignments.

questions.stem: A reviewer expected to see three separate SharePoint entitlements for an identity, but sees one access profile instead. The identity holds exactly the entitlements in that access profile. Why?
choices: Matching entitlements gave the identity the access profile, so they are certified as it
The campaign filter merged the entitlements into one item to reduce volume
The entitlements were marked privileged, which hides them inside access profiles in reviews
The reviewer lacks rights to see entitlements and can only see access profiles
questions.answer: Matching entitlements gave the identity the access profile, so they are certified as it
questions.explanation: When an identity's entitlements match an access profile, the identity is given that access profile and the entitlements are certified only as part of it. Campaign filters exclude items; they never merge them.

questions.stem: During a manager campaign, a manager says a former team member's account on the ticketing system is missing from her review. The account exists on the source but is uncorrelated. Why is it missing?
choices: Ticketing system sources can only be reviewed in role composition or source owner campaigns
Manager campaigns only include accounts on authoritative sources
Uncorrelated accounts belong to no identity, so identity-based reviews leave them out
The account was hidden because its entitlements have no descriptions
questions.answer: Uncorrelated accounts belong to no identity, so identity-based reviews leave them out
questions.explanation: Manager campaigns review the access of identities, and an uncorrelated account belongs to no identity. Missing descriptions make items harder to read but do not remove them.

questions.stem: An AD group was removed from a user by hand last week, but it still appears in today's campaign. The AD source was last aggregated ten days ago. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Campaigns always show access as it was at the start of the quarter
The group is protected by an SoD policy, which keeps it in reviews
The campaign uses tenant data from the last aggregation, which predates the removal
Manager campaigns read each account's access live from AD whenever a reviewer opens them
questions.answer: The campaign uses tenant data from the last aggregation, which predates the removal
questions.explanation: Campaigns reflect the access the tenant knows about, which is only as current as the last aggregation. Nothing reads access live from the target when a reviewer opens a campaign.

questions.stem: After a campaign, the audit team asks whether every revoke decision was actually carried out on the target sources. Which report BEST answers this?
choices: The Campaign Remediation Status report
The Identities Without Managers report
The Certification Sign Off report
The Campaign Composition report
questions.answer: The Campaign Remediation Status report
questions.explanation: The remediation status report tracks revoked items and their remediation. The sign off report shows who signed off, not whether access was removed.

questions.stem: A source owner campaign sent all reviews for the Oracle Financials source to a former IT manager who moved to marketing. What should the engineer fix before the next campaign?
choices: Change the IT manager's lifecycle state to inactive
Update the source owner on the Oracle Financials source configuration
Add a campaign filter that excludes the IT manager's identity
Remove the IT manager from the Cert Admin user level
questions.answer: Update the source owner on the Oracle Financials source configuration
questions.explanation: Source owner campaigns route reviews to the owner set on each source, so the owner must be corrected there. Changing his lifecycle state would disrupt his own access without fixing the routing.

questions.stem: Reviewers say the Department value shown for many identities in the campaign is wrong. The values come from an identity profile mapping that reads the wrong HR column. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Create a role composition campaign to review the Department attribute
Fix the identity profile mapping, process identities, then regenerate the campaign
Ask reviewers to note the correct department in the comments on each of their decisions
Edit the Department value inside the campaign for each identity
questions.answer: Fix the identity profile mapping, process identities, then regenerate the campaign
questions.explanation: Identity attributes come from identity profile mappings, so the mapping must be fixed and identities processed before regenerating. Campaign data cannot be edited per identity.

questions.stem: A manager campaign generated no reviews at all for 600 identities from a newly onboarded HR source. Their manager attribute is empty. What is the MOST likely root cause?
choices: Manager correlation is not configured on the new HR source
The new HR source is not set as the campaign's default reviewer
The new HR source has no account deletion threshold set
The new HR source uses a delimited file instead of a JDBC connector
questions.answer: Manager correlation is not configured on the new HR source
questions.explanation: Without manager correlation the identities have no manager, and identities without a manager are excluded from manager campaigns. The connector type is irrelevant to the manager relationship.

questions.stem: Put the steps for running a manager certification campaign in order.
items: Aggregate the in-scope sources so access data is current
Create the manager campaign with its deadline and any campaign filter
Review the generated preview and reassign certifications where needed
Start the campaign so reviewers are notified
Reviewers decide every item and sign off
Track revocations with the remediation status report
questions.explanation: Fresh data comes first, then the campaign is defined and its preview checked before it starts. Reviewers sign off to finalize decisions, and remediation is tracked last.

questions.stem: Match each business requirement to the campaign type that BEST fits it.

pairs.item: Managers confirm their direct reports' access
The owner of one licensed application reviews its access
Confirm a role still contains the right access
Review only identities returned by a precise query

questions.explanation: Each requirement maps to who reviews and what is reviewed. There is no lifecycle state campaign type; lifecycle state access is not certified that way.

questions.stem: An engineer is preparing a large manager campaign. Which TWO steps BEST improve the quality of reviews?
choices: Give entitlements clear display names and descriptions
Check the Identities Without Managers report and fix the gaps
Remove all campaign filters so every item is included
Set the deadline to one day so reviewers act quickly
Start the campaign a week after generating its preview
answers: Give entitlements clear display names and descriptions
Check the Identities Without Managers report and fix the gaps
questions.explanation: Readable entitlements and complete manager data help reviews reach the right people with understandable content. A week-old preview is stale and should be recreated.

questions.stem: When entitlement requests are enabled globally, an admin opens the reviewer list. Which reviewer option means the owner of the source the entitlement comes from?
choices: Governance Group
Source Owner
Entitlement Owner
Manager
questions.answer: Source Owner
questions.explanation: Source Owner sends entitlement requests to the owner of the entitlement's source. Entitlement Owner is the owner set on the entitlement itself.

questions.stem: A Helpdesk user requests the VPN Users access profile for an employee named Ana. The access profile requires Manager approval. Whose approval is needed?
choices: The VPN source owner
The Helpdesk user's manager
The access profile's primary owner
Ana's manager
questions.answer: Ana's manager
questions.explanation: The Manager option means the manager of the identity the access is being requested for. The requester's own manager is not involved.

questions.stem: An access profile has a primary owner and two additional owners. The business wants any one of the three to be able to approve requests. Which reviewer option should the engineer choose?
choices: All Owners
Additional Owners
Manager
Primary Owner
questions.answer: All Owners
questions.explanation: All Owners lets the primary owner or any additional owner approve. Additional Owners alone excludes the primary owner.

questions.stem: The Treasury Analyst role includes the Bank Portal access profile, which requires approval by its own owner. A user requests the Treasury Analyst role. Which approval process applies?
choices: No approval, because roles never require approval
Both the role's and the access profile's approval processes
The role's approval process, not the access profile's
The access profile's approval process, because it is more specific
questions.answer: The role's approval process, not the access profile's
questions.explanation: An access profile's approval process only applies when the access profile itself is requested; requests for a role use the role's approvals. They are not stacked together.

questions.stem: An engineer set approval on the Email Basic access profile, but new hires still receive it with no approval. The Active lifecycle state grants it. Why is there no approval?
choices: Lifecycle state and auto-assigned role access bypass approval
Lifecycle states always use the global approval settings instead
Approval only applies once the identity has been active for a day
The access profile's approvers must be in a governance group first
questions.answer: Lifecycle state and auto-assigned role access bypass approval
questions.explanation: Access profiles granted by lifecycle states or auto-assigned roles are provisioned without approval. Approval settings only apply to access requests.

questions.stem: An engineer wants an access profile's approvals handled by a workflow rather than by fixed reviewers. Which trigger must the workflow use to appear in the approval list?
choices: Access Request Submitted
Provisioning Completed
Account Aggregation Completed
Identity Attributes Changed
questions.answer: Access Request Submitted
questions.explanation: Only enabled workflows that use the Access Request Submitted trigger are offered for approval. The other triggers fire on events that are not request approvals.

questions.stem: An engineer edits an access profile for requests but leaves Require Approval switched off. What governs approval for requests of this access profile?
choices: The source owner automatically becomes the approver
Requests are blocked until an approver is configured
Requests are approved and provisioned with no checks
The tenant's global approval configuration still applies
questions.answer: The tenant's global approval configuration still applies
questions.explanation: If Require Approval is not chosen on the item, the global approval configuration still applies. It does not mean the request skips all approval.

questions.stem: Every entitlement on a mainframe source must require source owner approval, and the source has 4,000 entitlements. What is the MOST efficient way to configure this?
choices: Edit each entitlement's request settings one at a time
Set the source-level entitlement request configuration through the API
Bundle all 4,000 entitlements into a single requestable role with approval
Create one SoD policy that lists every mainframe entitlement
questions.answer: Set the source-level entitlement request configuration through the API
questions.explanation: The source-level entitlement request configuration acts like a global setting for that source's entitlements and can still be overridden per entitlement. Bundling everything into one role changes what users can request.

questions.stem: An access profile uses a governance group of five security analysts as its reviewer. How many of the analysts must approve a request?
choices: Any one member of the group
The group's designated owner only
A majority of the group
All five members of the group
questions.answer: Any one member of the group
questions.explanation: Only one identity in a governance group is required to approve on behalf of the group. Requiring everyone would be a multi-approver setup with separate steps.

questions.stem: Policy requires that the requester's manager approves first and the security team approves second for a privileged access profile. How should the engineer configure it?
choices: Add only the security governance group and include the manager in the group
Add the security governance group, then Manager, and order the group first
Add Manager and set an escalation chain that ends with the security team
Add Manager, then the security governance group, and order Manager first
questions.answer: Add Manager, then the security governance group, and order Manager first
questions.explanation: Multiple reviewers are asked in the configured order, so Manager must be listed before the governance group. An escalation chain only acts when approvers do not respond.

questions.stem: A request has three approval levels. The first approver approves, then the second approver denies. What happens?
choices: The access is provisioned because most approvers have not denied it
The review stops and the access is not provisioned
The request returns to the first approver to reconsider
The request moves on to the third approver for a final decision
questions.answer: The review stops and the access is not provisioned
questions.explanation: All required reviewers must approve, and a denial at any level stops the review. The third level is never reached.

questions.stem: An access profile's reviewers are Primary Owner first and Additional Owners second. When do the additional owners see a request?
choices: Only if the primary owner denies it
At the same time as the primary owner
Only after the request has timed out
Only after the primary owner has approved it
questions.answer: Only after the primary owner has approved it
questions.explanation: When the primary owner is the first reviewer, additional owners do not see the request until the primary owner approves. They are a second, sequential step.

questions.stem: An engineer wants pending approvals for an access profile to expire if no one acts on them. What is the longest timeout that can be set?
choices: 365 days
30 days
90 days
180 days
questions.answer: 90 days
questions.explanation: The Timeout field allows up to 90 days before a request expires. Longer values are not available.

questions.stem: On the approvals admin page, the assignee for a pending approval shows as Multiple. What does this MOST likely mean?
choices: The approval failed and was copied to every org admin in the tenant
The request contains several access items from different sources
The request was submitted for more than one identity
The approval is assigned to the members of a governance group
questions.answer: The approval is assigned to the members of a governance group
questions.explanation: A review assigned to a governance group is actually assigned to its members, so the assignee shows as Multiple. The members are listed on the Assignees tab.

questions.stem: A bank wants approvers of its wire-transfer access profile to prove who they are again at the moment they approve. What should the engineer enable?
choices: Required comments when the user requests access
An escalation chain that starts after one day
A second governance group as an extra approval level
Reauthenticated approvals for that access item
questions.answer: Reauthenticated approvals for that access item
questions.explanation: Reauthenticated approvals make reviewers reauthenticate when they approve sensitive or regulated items. An extra approval level adds a person but does not re-verify identity.

questions.stem: The owner of the Finance Reports access profile requests it for herself. She is the only configured reviewer. With default settings, who reviews the request?
choices: She approves it herself, because she is the configured reviewer
Her manager, because self-approval is not permitted
Any org admin, picked at random
The source owner of the reporting source
questions.answer: Her manager, because self-approval is not permitted
questions.explanation: By default the tenant does not permit self-approval, and an individual approval assigned to the requester is reassigned to their manager. The source owner is not part of that reassignment.

questions.stem: A requester belongs to the four-person governance group that approves the access profile she is requesting. What happens to the group's review?
choices: She is left out, and another group member must approve
The review is reassigned to the governance group owner's manager
She can approve it because the approval is assigned to the group
The whole group is skipped and the request is approved
questions.answer: She is left out, and another group member must approve
questions.explanation: For governance group approvals, the requester or recipient is omitted from the review so someone else in the group must act. Skipping the whole group would remove the control.

questions.stem: An engineer wants requests auto-approved when the configured reviewer is the requester, instead of being sent to the requester's manager. How is this enabled?
choices: Add each owner to a governance group that has only one member
Enable reauthenticated approvals for all of the owners' own access profiles
Turn off Require Approval on every access profile they own
Set the autoApprove option in the approval configuration through the API
questions.answer: Set the autoApprove option in the approval configuration through the API
questions.explanation: Automatic approval for self-assigned reviews is set with an API call that sets autoApprove to Direct or Indirect. Turning off approval would affect every requester.

questions.stem: An access profile requires Manager approval, but the recipient has no manager. No escalation chain or fallback approver is set. Who MOST likely receives the approval?
choices: The requester, who can then approve their own request
No one, so the request is denied at once
The owner of the requested access profile
The source owner of the first entitlement in the profile
questions.answer: The owner of the requested access profile
questions.explanation: When a reviewer cannot be resolved, the tenant tries the missing reviewer's manager, the escalation chain, the fallback approver and then the requested object's owner. Self-approval is never the outcome.

questions.stem: An approval has passed through every approver in its escalation chain and still nobody has acted. Who receives it next?
choices: The original requester
The first approver in the chain again
The fallback approver
The tenant's default support admin
questions.answer: The fallback approver
questions.explanation: A fallback approver receives a request once the full escalation chain has been tried with no action. Requests are not sent back to the requester.

questions.stem: Approvers should get a nudge every day starting two days after a request arrives, but the request must stay with them. What should the engineer configure?
choices: Escalations, not reminders
A second approval level
Reminders, not escalations
A shorter request timeout
questions.answer: Reminders, not escalations
questions.explanation: Reminders notify the same approver on a schedule, while escalations move the approval to others in the chain. A shorter timeout would make requests expire sooner, not nudge anyone.

questions.stem: An engineer is building the escalation chain for an access profile. Which reviewer categories can be added to the chain?
choices: Manager, Source Owner, Requester and Owners
Identity, Governance Group, Requester and Org Admin
Manager, Cert Admin, Helpdesk and a specific Identity
Manager, Identity, Governance Group and Owners
questions.answer: Manager, Identity, Governance Group and Owners
questions.explanation: The escalation chain accepts Manager, Identity, Governance Group and Owners. The requester is never an escalation target.

questions.stem: How does a conflicting access SoD policy decide that an identity is in violation?
choices: The identity holds any access item that is marked privileged
The identity holds access from both of the policy's two access lists
The identity requested access that its own manager later did not approve
The identity holds more than a set number of entitlements on one source
questions.answer: The identity holds access from both of the policy's two access lists
questions.explanation: An SoD policy has two lists, and a violation occurs when an identity has access in both. Privileged classification and access counts are separate concepts.

questions.stem: Which situation is the BEST candidate for an SoD policy rather than an approval rule?
choices: Every request for a sensitive database role needs approval from the DBA team
Contractors should lose all access on their end date
The same person should never both create vendors and approve vendor payments
New hires should automatically receive email and VPN access
questions.answer: The same person should never both create vendors and approve vendor payments
questions.explanation: SoD prevents toxic combinations of access held by one person. A single sensitive item is handled with approvals, and joiner or leaver access with lifecycle states.

questions.stem: An engineer is building an SoD policy's access lists. Which types of access items can be added to them?
choices: Entitlements, access profiles and roles
Roles and identity attributes
Sources, accounts and entitlements
Entitlements only
questions.answer: Entitlements, access profiles and roles
questions.explanation: SoD access lists can hold entitlements, access profiles and roles. Whole sources and identity attributes are not access items in a conflicting access policy.

questions.stem: An SoD policy's Violation Owner is set to None, and the tenant has no Violation Admin. Who is assigned the violations?
choices: The source owner of the first conflicting item
An org admin
Each violator's manager
The policy owner
questions.answer: An org admin
questions.explanation: With no violation owner, violations go to the Violation Admin, and without one, to an org admin. The policy owner is responsible for the policy, not its violations.

questions.stem: Risk wants SoD policies sorted by how serious a violation would be. Which policy setting supports this?
choices: The policy level, such as Critical, High, Medium or Low
The order the policies appear on the policies page
The size of the policy's two access lists
The policy's tags, set to a number from one to ten
questions.answer: The policy level, such as Critical, High, Medium or Low
questions.explanation: Each SoD policy has a level that classifies its risk, and policies can be filtered by level. Tags are free text and do not express risk.

questions.stem: The business accepts that two warehouse supervisors may hold conflicting access for 60 days while a compensating review is done each week. What should the engineer use?
choices: Change the policy level from High to Low
A mitigating control on the policy that expires after the agreed period
Disable the policy for 60 days and then enable it again once they finish
Remove the supervisors' conflicting access from List B
questions.answer: A mitigating control on the policy that expires after the agreed period
questions.explanation: Mitigating controls document accepted exceptions and expire after a set number of days. Disabling the policy hides every other violation as well.

questions.stem: A finance team lists 120 entitlements that must never be held together with a set of payment approval items. What should the engineer keep in mind while designing the policy?
choices: Each access list must contain exactly the same number of access items as the other
Each list holds at most 50 access items, so they must be grouped or split
Each SoD policy can only include entitlements from one source
Each SoD policy can only be evaluated against role memberships
questions.answer: Each list holds at most 50 access items, so they must be grouped or split
questions.explanation: SoD policies allow at most 50 access items per list and need at least one per list. Grouping entitlements into access profiles or roles, or splitting the policy, keeps within the limit.

questions.stem: An SoD policy uses the Block submission setting. A user submits a request that would conflict with it. What happens?
choices: The request is cancelled automatically
The request is sent to the violation owner for approval
The request is provisioned and a violation is logged
The request waits until a mitigating control is added
questions.answer: The request is cancelled automatically
questions.explanation: Block submission makes the system cancel access requests that conflict with the policy. Allow submission is the setting that routes conflicting requests to approvers.

questions.stem: An SoD policy uses Allow submission. A conflicting role request reaches the manager for approval. What does the manager see?
choices: A form asking the manager to name a mitigating control
Nothing, because SoD checks only run on a schedule
A notice that granting the request would cause an SoD violation
A request that has already been approved by the policy owner
questions.answer: A notice that granting the request would cause an SoD violation
questions.explanation: With Allow submission, conflicting requests go to the configured approvers, who are notified about the violation. Requesters also see the notice on their submitted requests.

questions.stem: A new SoD policy was just enabled. Thirty users already held both sides of the conflict before it existed. How will these existing violations be found?
choices: Automatically, the next time each user signs in
Only when each affected user requests new access
Only when the policy owner edits List A
By running the policy now or on a schedule
questions.answer: By running the policy now or on a schedule
questions.explanation: Request-time checks only cover new requests, so existing conflicts are found by running or scheduling the policy. Violations then appear on the Policy Violations page.

questions.stem: Compliance wants an email every Monday listing new violations of a payments SoD policy, even when there are none. What should the engineer configure?
choices: A policy schedule with subscribers and the no-violations email toggle on
A search subscription filtered on access requests
A workflow that runs whenever the policy is edited and emails the policy owner
An escalation chain on the policy's access lists
questions.answer: A policy schedule with subscribers and the no-violations email toggle on
questions.explanation: Policy schedules set the run time and subscribers, and a toggle controls whether an email is sent when there are no violations. Escalation chains belong to approvals, not SoD.

questions.stem: Auditors want the people who currently violate an SoD policy to have their access reviewed in a certification. What is the MOST direct way to do this?
choices: Export the violations and email them to each manager
Create a role composition campaign for the conflicting roles
Use the policy's Create Certification action
Create a manager campaign for every identity in the tenant
questions.answer: Use the policy's Create Certification action
questions.explanation: The SoD policy Actions menu includes Create Certification, which builds a review of the policy's violations. A tenant-wide manager campaign is far wider than the requirement.

questions.stem: A role assigned automatically by membership criteria gives a user access that conflicts with an SoD policy set to Block submission. How is this violation detected?
choices: The role assignment is blocked when the identity refresh runs
It is never detected, because roles are exempt from SoD
When the policy runs, because blocking only applies to access requests
The role assignment is cancelled and the role owner is notified
questions.answer: When the policy runs, because blocking only applies to access requests
questions.explanation: Block and Allow submission act on access requests; access given by automatic role assignment is found by running the policy. Roles can still be listed in SoD access lists.

questions.stem: A violation owner wants to know what the policy author recommends doing when a violation occurs. Where should the author have recorded this guidance?
choices: In the comments field of the policy's approval workflow for each request
In the policy's mitigation advice and remediation advice fields
In the policy's external reference tag
In the description of each entitlement listed in the policy's List A
questions.answer: In the policy's mitigation advice and remediation advice fields
questions.explanation: SoD policies include mitigation and remediation advice fields to guide whoever handles violations. Entitlement descriptions explain access, not what to do about conflicts.

questions.stem: Put the steps for creating and enforcing a conflicting access SoD policy in order.
items: Enter the policy details, owner, violation owner and level
Choose Block submission or Allow submission for access requests
Add conflicting access items to List A and List B
Review the policy and finish it
Enable the policy and run or schedule it to find existing violations
questions.explanation: Details and request behaviour come first on the policy details tab, then the two lists, review, enablement and a run that finds violations that existed before the policy.

questions.stem: Match each reviewer option to who approves the request.

pairs.match: The manager of the identity receiving the access
Any one member of the chosen group
The primary owner or any additional owner
The owner set on the requested entitlement

targets_extra: The manager of the person who submitted the request
questions.explanation: Each option resolves to a specific approver. Manager means the recipient's manager, not the requester's manager.

questions.stem: A requester is listed as the only individual reviewer for the access profile she requests. Which TWO statements describe default behaviour?
choices: Self-approval is not permitted by default
The approval is reassigned to her manager
The request is approved automatically
The request is cancelled with an SoD violation
The approval is sent to every org admin
answers: Self-approval is not permitted by default
The approval is reassigned to her manager
questions.explanation: The tenant blocks self-approval by default and reassigns an individual approval to the requester's manager. Auto-approval needs an explicit API setting.
